newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts close up on US data, curve flattening.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts close up on US data, curve flattening.

text.p: 1620 GMT - UK gilts follow US Treasuries higher on weaker than expected CPI data suggesting US inflation remains subdued. Flattening trades in gilts ahead of monetary meeting on Wednesday, despite growing expectations of no rate cut. * March gilt future settles 7/32 up at 109-24.
The data eased fears of an inflation revival in the U.S., making an imminent rise in the Fed funds rate less likely.
The 30-year Treasury bond rose a full point in early trade to 96-17/32, dragging the gilt market up with it.
"There were some short positions in the U.S. which had to be covered after some people got caught by the CPI data," said one London trader. "That short covering forced us up."

Dealers said the gilt curve flattened slightly on Tuesday although a rise in interest rates after Wednesday's monetary policy meeting between the Chancellor and the Bank of England governor is seen as less likely.
The British Retail Consortium's December sales monitor, released overnight, helped allay fears of a rate rise after the meeting, which is due to start at around 1500 GMT on Wednesday.
It said like-for-like sales in the UK grew 4.3 percent in value in December, down from November's 4.9 percent rate and October's 5.9 percent.
Economists said the survey, along with the recent weaker than expected CBI distributive trades survey, dampened fears of a consumer-led boom in 1997.
Dealers said there was some scope for the short end to rally slightly on Wednesday if rates are left on hold.
"But if they do raise them the short end will snap back big time and the curve will flatten dramatically," one trader said.
November average earnings data and December jobless figures, due at 0930 on Wednesday, will likely be overshadowed by the monetary meeting.
"No-one will care about the unemployment data unless it's wildly different from expectations," one trader said.
According to a Reuter survey, economists expect unemployment to fall by 30,000 in December after November's record 96,000 plunge. Average earnings growth is seen unchanged at 4.0 percent in November.
The March short sterling contract settled one basis point lower on Tuesday at 93.46.
The 10-year gilt/Bund spread widened slightly to 191 basis points from 190 at the open.
